notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0002] Guard division with a zero-total check: For weighted-average or ratio computations, compute the denominator first and return the module's zero constant when it is zero.
  Compute total_quantity (or equivalent denominator) before dividing; if it equals 0, return ZERO rather than dividing. This satisfies the empty-input spec and prevents ZeroDivisionError.
- [rb-0006] Inspect existing modules for error codes and helpers before implementing: Reading models.py, errors.py, money.py, and sibling functions revealed the exact BillingError codes and helpers to reuse.
  Before writing a new function, read the related models, error definitions, and neighboring functions in the same file. Reusing established error codes (invalid_state, invalid_quantity, negative_amount) and helpers (to_money, ZERO) keeps behavior consistent with hidden tests.
- [rb-0001] Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal arithmetic: When implementing monetary calculations, wrap raw values with the module's existing to_money/round_money/ZERO helpers instead of using plain Decimal or float.
  Inspect the money module first and route all arithmetic through its helpers (to_money on inputs, round_money on results, ZERO as the sum seed). This keeps rounding policy consistent and avoids float contamination.
- [rb-0003] Read tests and models before editing: Before writing the implementation, inspect the target test file, models, and money module to learn exact signatures, field names, and expected return types.
  Cat the relevant test and model files in the same step as the source file. This reveals field names (e.g. line.quantity, line.unit_price), expected types, and edge cases, letting the first attempt pass without review feedback.
- [rb-0004] Reject bools when validating integer inputs: Python's bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(True, int) is True; explicitly exclude bools when requiring a positive integer.
  When validating that a value is a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0`. Without the bool guard, True/False would silently pass as 1/0.
- [rb-0005] Normalize money via to_money before sign checks: Convert unit_price with the project's to_money helper before comparing against ZERO so strings/floats are handled consistently.
  Call the existing money-normalization helper (e.g. to_money) on raw price input, then compare the resulting Decimal to ZERO. This accepts string/float inputs uniformly and avoids float comparison pitfalls.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing.
[team convention] Write the amount in audit entries as float(amount): the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.

item.title: Check idempotency key before any state validation
item.description: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit trail first and return the original result early, before validating payment state or amounts.
item.content: Scan audit.events(<event_name>) for a matching idempotency_key at the very top of the function and return the original record unchanged. Doing this before state checks prevents spurious errors on retries (e.g. a payment already 'refunded' would otherwise fail the captured-state check).

item.title: Inspect sibling modules for undocumented team conventions
item.description: The first attempt missed idempotency_key, approved_by, and float(amount) audit conventions that were visible in existing modules like payments.py and audit.py.
item.content: Before implementing a new function, read analogous functions in sibling modules (payments.py, audit.py) to infer required keyword-only params, error codes, and audit field formats. These conventions are often not stated in the issue but are enforced by hidden tests.

item.title: Use money helpers and float for audit amounts
item.description: Normalize amounts with to_money/round_money, compare against ZERO, and write float(amount) into audit entries because the ledger JSON importer rejects Decimal.
item.content: Convert inputs via round_money(to_money(amount)), reject non-positive amounts, and accumulate refunded_amount with the same rounding. Always pass float(amount) (and float of running totals) to audit.record to satisfy the ledger service importer.
